✳ INFORMATION FOR SCHOOLS

ROBLOX BUILD DAY

Bring creative problem-solving into the classroom.

Build Day gives students a practical reason to learn Roblox Studio—the free tool used to create Roblox games and experiences. Over one online week, beginners plan, build, test, and share one small playable project.

Request school information ↗View the schedule ↓
5 daysMonday–Friday challenge
Beginner-readyNo previous building experience required
Free eventSchools still plan devices, accounts, and staffing
Self-pacedNo continuous attendance or large live session required

01 / LEARNING THROUGH MAKING

A small game becomes a reason to think, test, and explain.

Intended outcomes—not guaranteed results or curriculum claims.

01

Plan an idea

Students choose a theme, sketch one player goal, and write a simple build plan.

Artifact: one-sentence concept + sketch
02

Design an experience

They shape a small space and decide what the player can do, see, and discover.

Artifact: first playable environment
03

Test and improve

They playtest, notice what is confusing, and make at least one purposeful change.

Artifact: tested build + change note
04

Communicate the work

They submit a link and briefly explain the idea, contribution, and next step.

Artifact: project link + reflection
Teamwork option: students may work alone or in small teams. A team can divide planning, building, testing, and explaining while still submitting one shared project.

02 / THE WEEK

One milestone per day. One playable project by Friday.

EVENT FORMAT

The challenge is self-paced. The Monday theme, Friday submission deadline, and post-event showcase are the event anchors. The classroom arrangement below is a suggested way to fit the work into a school timetable—not a required live schedule.

MONDAYTheme + start

Students receive the creative theme, open a beginner Studio activity, and choose an idea.

TUESDAYBuild a place

Block out a small world, room, or course with a short tutorial.

WEDNESDAYAdd a goal

Add one interaction such as collect, reach, race, explore, or solve.

THURSDAYTest + improve

Playtest, fix one issue, and add one detail that makes the project personal.

FRIDAYSubmit

Send the project link and a short reflection before the confirmed deadline.

Suggested classroom arrangement

For example: introduce the theme during a short Monday lesson, offer one or two class work periods Tuesday–Thursday, and reserve a brief Friday submission check. Students can continue independently outside those periods if permitted.

Scheduled sessions: none are currently confirmed. [Optional live help, resource links, and exact deadlines TBC.]

03 / PREPARE TO PARTICIPATE

A clear checklist before the week begins.

Participation is free; school setup still takes planning.

Technology

  • Roblox accounts for participating students
  • Computers capable of running Roblox Studio
  • Roblox Studio installed or approved by school IT
  • Network, filtering, and account permissions checked

[Minimum specifications, managed-device instructions, and software approval route TBC.]

People & time

  • A teacher or school team decides when students may work
  • Time for a Monday introduction and Friday submission check
  • Clear expectations for solo or small-team work
  • Planning lead time for permissions and family communication

[Teacher training, organizer support, and expected student time commitment TBC.]

School decisions

  • Confirm eligibility and participation permissions
  • Choose how project links will be collected
  • Decide whether students can view the online showcase
  • Share the school’s supervision and reporting process

The school remains responsible for its own technology approvals, staffing, supervision, and safeguarding decisions.

04 / SAFETY, SUPERVISION & INCLUSION

Make room for different learners and different finishes.

Build Day is designed to welcome beginners, students with different levels of access, and projects at different stages. A playable first version is a valid finish; no student needs to compete for the “best” game.

SupervisionSchools decide who supervises students and how participation fits their policies. No organizer-provided supervision is confirmed.
SharingSchools decide which project links and student names may be shared. Showcase access and moderation arrangements are [TBC].
InclusionOffer the same milestones with flexible pacing, accessible instructions, team roles, and alternatives for students who cannot finish a full build.

CLARITY MATTERS

What is confirmed?

Confirmed: free online format, Monday–Friday flow, beginner focus, solo or small-team participation, Friday submission, and an online showcase after submissions.

Needs organizer input: dates, eligibility policy, resource links, submission platform, showcase access, moderation, safeguarding contact, accommodations, and school support.

05 / SCHOOL FAQ

Practical answers for planning conversations.

Use the information request below to ask for the details your board, principal, IT team, or families need.

What does it cost?+
Event participation is free. Schools should plan for devices, software access, staff time, supervision, and any local permissions.
Does a teacher need Roblox Studio experience?+
No previous building experience is required for students. Teacher preparation resources and any organizer support are [TBC].
Can students participate without a full class timetable?+
Yes. The event is self-paced Monday–Friday. Schools can suggest work periods, while students may progress during approved independent time.
Who supervises students?+
The school is responsible for supervision and its safeguarding procedures. Build Day does not currently confirm a supervised live session.
What happens when a student does not finish?+
Students may submit an unfinished but playable project, a smaller version, or a documented next step. The showcase should celebrate learning and effort, not only polish.
